articles.title: Unusual Jets stat offer needed early-season optimism
articles.summary: This stat really puts the Jets' improvements from last season into picture.
articles.body:
One of the things that makes the NFL season what it is is the fact that teams can never get too high or too low.

That's exactly what the New York Jets are experiencing. The heartbreaking 20-17 overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers is already in the past as head coach Aaron Glenn prepares his team for a Week 3 trip to tackle the Detroit Lions , where he'll face a team he once helped lead after spending four seasons as their defensive coordinator.

The Jets don't have much time to dwell on what happened Sunday, but we do have a moment to look back at two bizarre and surprisingly encouraging statistics that emerged from the home opener.

ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter pointed out that New York ran 55 plays with the lead during its Week 1 victory over the Tennessee Titans . He states, for perspective, the Jets ran just 66 total plays with a lead during all of the 2025 season.

Think about that for a moment. After one game, the Jets had already been ahead for nearly as many offensive snaps as they were during the entirety of the previous season.

Not to be outdone, there is another stat for more context here, noting that the Jets have now run more plays with a lead through two games this season than they did during all of 2025.

That's not going to make the Packers loss any less frustrating, but it does provide another indication that this Jets team is operating from a much different position than last year's group.

The Jets are finding themselves in unfamiliar territory

The second statistic is even more interesting when viewed through the lens of what happened against Green Bay . The Jets led the Packers 17-7 in the fourth quarter and ultimately lost. That is obviously the part everyone remembers, but there is another side to it: New York keeps putting itself in position to control games.

For a team that struggled so badly to play from ahead last season, the early-season transformation is striking. The Jets have not figured out how to consistently finish those games yet, but they are putting themselves in the position to have that problem in the first place.

None of this will help the Jets win Sunday in Detroit. It won't erase the fourth-quarter collapse against Green Bay, either. Still, after the emotional toll of Week 2, we'll take our silver linings wherever we can find them.

articles.title: Climate emergency declaration scrapped by Calderdale Council
articles.summary: Two members of the public are removed from the gallery during the Calderdale Council debate.
articles.body:
Calderdale Council has voted to scrap its climate emergency declaration several years after it was introduced.

The decision was made by the Reform UK-led administration, despite its leader Dan Sutherland having proposed the original declaration when he was a Labour councillor in 2019, saying immediate action was needed.

Protesters gathered outside Halifax Town Hall before Wednesday's meeting, with two members of the public removed from the gallery during the debate.

Reform councillor Connor Dent told the meeting scrapping the declaration was not because "we should care less about our environment", but questioned whether it gave "the best possible outcomes" for residents and the environment.

During the meeting, a 90-year-old protester was among those escorted out by security staff after shouting that scientists had said there was a climate emergency and it should not be ignored.

After another two interruptions, the public gallery was ordered to be cleared, but eventually remaining members of the public were allowed to stay on the basis that they would not further interrupt the debate.

The decision in Calderdale follows similar moves by other Reform-led councils , including Wakefield, which recently voted to "undeclare" the climate emergency the authority had unanimously backed in 2019.

Outlining Calderdale's proposals, Dent said every pound spent by the council must be justified, and environmental policy must deliver real benefits and not just look good on paper.

He said changes shaped by the policy, including building cycle lanes, had caused congestion and a loss of parking spaces which residents had questioned.

He added that the expected increases in the level of cycling had not materialised.

Dent also said the policy had "disconnected" from local worries, citing a battery energy storage plant being given planning permission at Holmfield in Halifax.

Supporting him, Reform councillor Mike Payne said practical, proportionate, safe environmental measures that benefited residents would be supported, but not "virtue signalling".

Opposing the motion, Labour councillor Scott Patient said Reform-led councils were following the party line.

He said the declaration had helped secure £150m for projects, including home insulation, flood resilience and public buildings, and argued that any savings from scrapping it would be minimal.

Supporting him, Councillor Martin Hey, leader of the Green Party group, said that climate initiatives had helped create a green economy worth millions of pounds, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service .

Before the meeting, councillors were lobbied by residents and groups, including Green New Deal and Extinction Rebellion, who voiced concerns about the council's withdrawal from the commitment.

One campaigner, Ali Bath, from Extinction Rebellion, said the previous administration had tried to tackle the issue, but that was now under threat.

She added: "There are huge impacts on our everyday lives and I don't know how communities are going to cope. I don't think people are prepared."

articles.title: Falcons and Packers both searching for answers heading into 'Thursday Night Football' in NFL Week 3
articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. takes over for Cooper Rush as the Falcons try to unlock Bijon Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts in a stalling offense.
articles.body: Week 3 is here in the NFL, and I really hope it is nothing like Week 2. Let’s toss aside the sports betting aspect for a moment, but we saw three young quarterbacks- Caleb Williams, Jaxon Dart, and Jayden Daniels- get injured. Timetables are uncertain for some returns, but either way, football is better with primary quarterbacks available. We have two in tonight's game between the Falcons and Packers. The Atlanta Falcons are getting back a starting quarterback of their own. Well… kind of. They are getting Michael Penix Jr. back, but he is returning and taking over for Cooper Rush. The original starter was supposed to be Tua Tagovailoa, but he’s been unavailable all season. Penix Jr. will have his hands full trying to figure out what to do with this offense. They don’t lack playmakers - Bijan Robinson is solid, Drake London is a really good receiver, and Kyle Pitts (although drafted too high) is still a solid option. In the first two games, the Falcons were essentially outmatched. Is that because Rush was under center? In game one, they scored 13 points, but last week they could only get 3 points against a team that almost allowed 60 points in Week 1. The offense wasn’t terrible by some measures - they had 17 first downs, one fewer than the Panthers. However, they had three turnovers; if they shore those up, maybe it’s a more competitive game. MICHAEL PENIX JR. OFFICIALLY NAMED FALCONS STARTER FOR A SHORT-WEEK TRIAL BY FIRE AGAINST PACKERS On the other side of the field is a team with more than enough questions of their own. The Packers are 1-1, but it wasn’t easy to get that victory. They had to go into New Jersey to face the Jets, and they were forced into an overtime game with them. They came out on top 20-17. I don’t want to act like we should be impressed or pleased with that performance, but perhaps it is something to build on, and now they get their first home game. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! In Week 1 it wasn’t much better for the Packers. Green Bay was fine against the Vikings, at least for the first half of the game. They struggled to get much going against the Minnesota defense and gave up their lead in the second half. It wasn’t just that; they barely could score and couldn’t keep Carson Wentz from marching down the field. I do blame the front office. I’m not exactly sure that Jordan Love is an elite quarterback, but his receiving options certainly don’t help make him much better. Couple that with Josh Jacobs being out, and this offense should be expected to struggle. articles.title: Hundreds turn out for Bristol's Jacob Elordi lookalike contest
articles.summary: The contest, organised by a group from the University of Bristol, included an Australian accent round.
articles.body:
Hundreds of people turned out to watch a Jacob Elordi lookalike contest which saw youngsters don their finest tote bags and slouchy sweatshirts.

The event, which took place on College Green, was organised by Overheard at UoB - a social media community dedicated to life at the University of Bristol.

Acclaimed Australian actor Elordi is best known for his roles in The Kissing Booth, Saltburn, Frankenstein, Wuthering Heights, Priscilla and the HBO series Euphoria.

Despite some worthy competitors performing their best catwalk struts and Australian accents, the title was awarded to a 17-year-old girl who did not want to be named.

An estimated 500 people showed up to watch the contest unfold.

Jamie Crook, who recently moved to the city from Oxford, said he was shocked at the large turnout and "had jelly legs the whole time".

He said: "I loved it, it was so fun. I'm still kind of shaking now.

"I think it's a really good way to make friends and get to know people.

"I feel like one of the most famous blokes in Bristol for a day, which is an experience."

NHS staff investigated over access to dead teenager's medical records

Mayor believes mass transit system is coming

Hovis workers pause strike after fresh pay deal

The veterinary medicine student even took the time to thank his doppelganger directly, acknowledging the boost to his street cred.

"For the better half of seven years, since the Kissing Booth came out, Jacob Elordi has carried my dating career," he laughed.

"Every time he cuts my hair I show him a picture of Jacob Elordi and he just sorts it out.

Crook explained the accent round was his downfall.

He blamed his croaky impersonation on a lingering "fresher's flu".

Joey Lush secured second place in the competition after trawling through Pinterest for outfit inspiration and "grabbing a tote bag from the fresher's fair".

He said: "He's a very stylish guy, so I tried my best.

"I did not realise what I was signing up for - I was a bit nervous going up."

"The winner did an amazing job," he said. "I'm so okay with it, I lost fair and square.

"I saw her in the line and she was the only one I wouldn't have been... hurt about losing to.

"I think it was her moustache that sold it."

articles.title: PGA Tour Golfer's Caddie Who Quit Mid-Round Explains Reason for Dramatic Split
articles.summary: During the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship in Asheville last week, fans witnessed a live breakup between a golfer and caddie.
articles.body:
During the PGA Tour's Biltmore Championship in Asheville last week, fans witnessed a live breakup between a golfer and caddie.

Alejandro Tosti's caddie, Cliff Ellis, dropped his bag, removed his caddie bib and left on the 18th hole of the first round.

While the two reportedly had been at odds before the tournament started, Ellis gave a more in-depth answer as to why he left so suddenly.

According to MondayQ's Ryan French , Ellis had frustrations with Tosti regarding their financial arrangement, but there was also tension with how Ellis was treated on the course and in practice.

Ellis told French that during the Charles Schwab Challenge, Tosti instructed him, "Don't do anything unless I tell you," but became angry and used the F-word multiple times when Ellis didn't immediately pull the flag on the 14th hole.

At the Rocket Classic in Detroit, Ellis said Tosti "went crazy" multiple times during the first round. He said Tosti slammed his clubs on the ground and hit penalty-area stakes in anger. Ellis added that Tosti at one point threw his bag and nearly hit him, though Ellis clarified that he didn't believe the throw was targeted towards him.

According to French, Ellis said a PGA Tour official warned Tosti that he could be suspended if he had another outburst like the one he had in Detroit.

Ellis said issues arose between him and Tosti once again in Asheville last week, specifically noting that he faced criticism for where he placed Tosti's bag.

"Are you going to make me walk to the locker room for my clubs?" Ellis recalled Tosti saying.

After a few missed shots during the first round, Ellis said he encouraged Tosti to let the previous mistakes go and focus on the ones ahead. Tosti confronted him about it on the next tee.

"Don't do that again, or I'll get really angry," Ellis recalled Tosti saying.

Later on, after a back-and-forth about Ellis including an umbrella in the golf bag, he said Tosti repeatedly called him a "dumbass."

The boiling point was on the 18th hole, where Ellis threatened to drop the bag multiple times without receiving much of a response from Tosti. Ultimately, Ellis decided he was done and told Tosti, "Good luck," as he made his way to the parking lot.

articles.title: Judge unseals files in Josh Jacobs case; record requests can proceed
articles.summary: A judge lifted the order sealing records in the Josh Jacobs case, allowing for potential public access to files.
articles.body:
A Brown County Circuit Court Judge on Sept. 24 lifted his temporary order sealing the records in the Josh Jacobs case and said the legal process should play out.

Green Bay Packers running back Jacobs pleaded no contest on Sept. 10 in Brown County Circuit Court to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges stemming from a May 23 incident in Hobart with an ex-girlfriend.

Judge Marc Hammer said Wisconsin open records law favors public access, but it will be up to the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department to apply a balancing test between the rights of the public, the defendant and the victim in deciding whether to release records. Parties can then appeal the decision, in which case it will end up back in court.

Hobart/Lawrence Police Chief Michael Renkas said the department denied a number of requests so far based on the temporary order to seal the record. Hammer said his order will be vacated by Sept. 25, and new open records requests can be made.

Jacobs missed Packers games so far this season because he is on the commissioner's exempt list, which means he cannot play or practice with the team. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network/ESPN reported on Sept. 13 that the NFL wants to see security video from the home during the incident before deciding on how long Jacobs should be suspended.

The Press-Gazette and other media filed open records requests for the video and other documents, which were denied under the temporary sealed-records order.

Attorneys for the victim submitted a proposed order permanently sealing the records on Sept. 15, citing state statute and Marsy's Law, which ensures that victims of crime have equal, constitutional rights on the same level as those accused and convicted of crimes. Hammer denied that request, preferring that the process continue under open records law rather than through the criminal case.

The victim, who has not been named, is concerned that personally identifying information could be made public. Hammer suggested such information could be removed without the entire record being sealed.

Jacobs has not requested the record be permanently sealed.

For the battery charge , Hammer on Sept. 10 accepted Jacobs' plea and the mutually recommended fine of $1,000 and court costs. For the criminal damage to property charge, he was ordered to not have contact with the victim, pay restitution, attend counseling and be under supervision for one year.

articles.title: Sex offender bailed to flat near playground
articles.summary: Victims of Zapher Dogen were living close to the 32-year-old, who admitted multiple offences.
articles.body:
A sex offender jailed for taking thousands of pictures of children and using AI software to "nudify" them was repeatedly allowed to return to his home overlooking the playground he targeted.

It meant victims of Zafer Dogan, from Enfield in north London, were living close to the 32-year-old, who admitted multiple offences.

Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley spoke outside Wood Green Crown Court after Dogan was jailed for two years and four months, where Sir Mark criticised the "unfathomable decisions" of the justice system.

"The children should be put first, not the paedophile," he said.

Dogan, who works as a mechanic, previously pleaded guilty to multiple offences, including making indecent images of children.

According to the police, he had taken more than 5,000 pictures, many from his bedroom window.

The mother of a victim under the age of eight described feeling "helpless", adding: "Our lives will never be the same again and I can't do anything about it all because one man exploited my child."

The mother of a teenage victim said it was as if she had been "punched in the gut" when police officers told her what had happened.

She added: "I'm really worried that my daughter's photos are online and other paedophiles have them."

Sir Mark said: "Prosecutors rightly opposed bail on multiple occasions, building on officers' clear assessments of the great risk he posed, and yet bail decisions were ultimately made that prioritised the offender's interests over the safety and the peace of mind of the victims.

"A victim and their family found themselves living in close proximity to a man who had admitted targeting them.

"They were so fearful, they ultimately felt forced to move to distant temporary accommodation, disrupting their lives and disrupting their children's lives, simply to escape being in the neighbourhood of the offender."

He also criticised "some grossly irresponsible technology and AI companies".

He said: "Dogan voyeuristically photographed children known to him before using an AI photo-editing technology to manipulate those images for his own sexual gratification. Companies must do more to prevent their platforms and tools from being used to facilitate sexual offending and harm.

"Innovation cannot come at the expense of public safety, and industry has a clear responsibility to help prevent these technologies being exploited by predators.

"Victims, in this case extremely young children and their families, deserve better from both the tech companies and the criminal justice system."

articles.title: Open de France: Michael Kim leads after 'dream start' as Matt Fitzpatrick impresses on low-scoring day at Le Golf National
articles.summary: English duo Matt Fitzpatrick and Sam Bairstow two behind early leader Michael Kim at Le Golf National; Tommy Fleetwood and Viktor Hovland among the other Ryder Cup stars in action; watch live on Friday from 12.30pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Kim carded eight birdies, including four of his first six holes, to post a bogey-free 63 on a low-scoring opening day and grab a two-shot advantage.

The American - beginning on the back nine - followed successive birdies from the 11th by adding two more from the 14th, then ended a run of pars by picking up a shot at the par-four first.

Kim failed to take advantage of the par-five third but added back-to-back birdies from the fifth to move top of the leaderboard, then doubled his lead over the chasing pack - including Fitzpatrick - by picking up a shot at the par-five ninth.

"Just a dream start," Kim said. "All parts of my game were really good, especially my irons and my putting. I couldn't have asked for a better start."

Fitzpatrick also made a blemish-free start, posting six birdies in a six-under 65, with the Englishman one of seven players sharing second after the opening round.

Thriston Lawrence was within one of the lead until a final-hole bogey dropped him back to six under, with Ryder Cup hopeful Kristoffer Reitan and England's Sam Bairstow also two back.

Australian Jason Scrivener and Italian duo Gerogio De Leo and Matteo Manassero are the others alongside Fitzpatrick in tied-second, with Ryder Cup vice-captain Edoardo Molinar three strokes back on five under.

"Really good day," Fitzpatrick said. "Great start to the week and relatively stress-free, which is always nice - particularly around this golf course."

Viktor Hovland is four off the early lead alongside American Ryan Gerard while Tommy Fleetwood - part of Europe's Ryder Cup-winning team at this venue in 2018 - started with a two-under 69.

Manuel Elvira, who double-bogeyed the 72nd hole to miss out on BMW PGA Championship victory on Sunday, sits second-bottom of the leaderboard after a nine-over 80.

articles.title: NFL Week 3 expert picks for Packers vs. Falcons on TNF
articles.summary: Who are the experts taking in the Packers vs. Falcons in Week 3 primetime showdown?
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers might have needed a 10-point comeback at MetLife Stadium to stun the New York Jets and avoid an 0-2 start just four days ago, but the vast majority of experts picking NFL games still believe the Packers will take down the Atlanta Falcons on "Thursday Night Football" to open Week 3.

A victory would improve the Packers to 2-1 going into a long weekend of rest and recovery. But Matt LaFleur's team has to first take care of business in the home opener at Lambeau Field, and there are no simple victories when a team has as many issues as the Packers appear to have through two weeks. Then again, the Falcons are 0-2, coming off a 31-point loss and on the road during a short week.

A review of the Week 3 expert picks of Packers vs. Falcons on TNF:

Of the six experts at USA Today , five picked the Packers.

From Davis: "The Packers know all too well what it's like to try and endure without your most important players at the start of the season, and they'll still be without OLB Micah Parsons and RB Josh Jacobs . But at least they'll finally be home at Lambeau Field, not the ideal environment for Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. to attempt to salvage what may already be a lost season in Atlanta … Though watching him and his talented offensive mates try should at least be entertaining."

Of the 11 experts at ESPN , all 11 picked the Packers.

Of the five experts at NFL.com , all five picked the Packers.

From Cersosimo: "The Packers, lucky to eke out a victory in New York to avoid falling to 0-2, finally return to beloved Lambeau Field, where they have won each of their last 13 home openers. I have concerns about Jordan Love 's O-line, which just lost starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele for the season and has others banged up (OG Aaron Banks , OT Anthony Belton and backup OL Donovan Jennings ). Love has already taken seven sacks (tied for third-most), faced the fifth-highest pressure rate in the NFL this season (42.3%) and is tied for the most unblocked pressures faced (12), per NFL Pro. How Matt LaFleur game plans for his shorthanded offense against a Falcons defense that ranks first against the run, ninth on third down and in the red zone and has generated pressure on 41.5 percent on dropbacks (seventh in the NFL, per Next Gen Stats) could tell part of Thursday night's story. Not having CB A.J. Terrell hurts Atlanta's chances of slowing Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , but having Michael Penix Jr. under center should be a boon for that team. Even if he's still knocking off the rust, this should look like a more competent unit, one that's better-suited to get Bijan Robinson , Drake London and Kyle Pitts more involved. These are two flawed teams, and though I think we'll see an improved Falcons outfit, Green Bay has a much-needed home-field edge and a defense that's playing with confidence with budding star Lukas Van Ness at the forefront. Clean up the penalties and this could be a turning point for the Pack."

Of the eight experts at MMQB , all eight picked the Packers.

Of the seven experts at The Athletic , all seven picked the Packers.

Of the seven experts at CBS Sports , six picked the Packers.

From Prisco: "This will be Michael Penix back in at quarterback for the Falcons, who badly need it. The Packers rallied to beat the Jets last week, thanks to the defense. That defense will play well here as well. Jordan Love gets it going if the banged-up line can hold up. I think they will."

Of the nine experts at SB Nation , eight picked the Packers.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: Scottie Scheffler, Sam Burns sneak through tough opening round as U.S. takes early lead at Medinah
articles.summary: The U.S. took a 3-2 lead over the International team thanks to a late push from Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns in Chicago.
articles.body:
Nobody can legitimately question how good of a golfer Scottie Scheffler is. He's the top-ranked golfer in the world for a reason, and has absolutely dominated the PGA Tour over the last several years.

But Scheffler's struggles on the international stage, a trend he can't seem to shake, continued on Thursday at Medinah Country Club in Chicago.

Scheffler was in the opening group at the 2026 Presidents Cup on Thursday, playing alongside Sam Burns in the first of five four-ball matches against the International team. The two managed to sneak out a 1-up win over Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, thanks to a huge save at the 17th, to get the United States on the board. It was also the first Presidents Cup or Ryder Cup match that Burns and Scheffler have won playing together.

By the end of the day, the U.S. took a 3-2 lead over the International team ahead of the foursomes matches on Friday. They've led after the opening session in 12 of the 16 Presidents Cups.

"We just did our best to stay in it," Scheffler said. "I felt like both teams got off to pretty hot starts today and we cooled off a little bit off that."

Scheffler opened the day with a walk-in birdie. But that was about his only highlight. Lee and Im quickly tied the match back up as Scheffler struggled to get much of anything going. He missed the green at the short par-3 7th and hit his tee shot into the crowd, for example, and couldn't get many putts to fall the rest of the way.

That largely left Burns as the one to try and hold things down. He sank a big birdie putt at the 9th to keep the match tied as they made the turn, and Lee and Im missed three straight birdie looks of their own that would have given them their first lead of the day. They finally jumped ahead of Burns and Scheffler on the 13th after Scheffler missed a 3-footer for birdie, though Burns made a putt on the 14th to even things up once again.

Scheffler got a 4-foot par putt to fall on the 17th, while Im missed a similar look in a rough mistake, to finally put the Americans in the lead for good. Scheffler had to save par after landing in the bunker at the 18th, however, to avoid splitting the point.

Scheffler's record on the international stage is lagging behind his other accomplishments. He's got a 3-6-3 record at the Ryder Cup, and he entered this week with a 3-5-1 record in Presidents Cup matches. Scheffler has never won a Presidents Cup singles match, either, though he's 2-0-1 in those at the Ryder Cup.

Scheffler and Burns, who are very good friends off the course, were a combined 0-3-1 when paired together at the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup before Thursday's win. Not great.

Luckily for Scheffler and the Americans, they're now in the lead after the first day in Chicago. Just not by much.

"I saw those guys competing their asses off out there," U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker said. "I'm really proud of them. A session win is a session win, we're going to take it any way we can get it. So happy for Scottie and Sam to go out there in that lead match and get that big win for us to lead us off.

"This is a long week. This is one session. We've got four more to go. Just proud of the way these guys started us off."

While the Scheffler-Burns group was slow, two pairs of Americans wasted no time in their matches behind them.

Justin Thomas and rookie Jackson Koivun rolled to a 4&3 win over Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria in the third match of the day. Koivun made three birdies on the front side to grab a lead almost immediately, and Koivun — who only made his PGA Tour debut mid-season earlier this year — looked comfortable out there.

Thomas then sank a birdie putt of his own from off the green at the 14th to push their lead back to three, which was enough to carry them to the early win. Thomas has now won his last seven four-ball matches at the Presidents Cup, which is tied for the all-time record. And at 21, Koivun is now the second-youngest American behind only Jordan Spieth to win a Presidents Cup match.

Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa cruised to a similar 3&2 win over Ryan Fox and Adam Scott. Clark went 4-under on the front nine himself, which was more than enough to keep Fox and Scott at bay. Clark then pushed their lead to three with a birdie on the 15th, which allowed them to end the match on the following hole.

Scott is playing in his 12th career Presidents Cup, and Thursday was his 55th overall match, both of which tied the all-time record with Phil Mickelson.

While they were in the last and slowest group of the day, Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim had little issue getting past Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay, winning 3&2 to secure an easy point for the Internationals.

They went 2-up through their first two holes to take control of the match almost instantly. While Cantlay and Gotterup rallied briefly — they made three birdies in a four-hole stretch to tie things up — that was all they could do. Cantlay became a non-factor the rest of the way while Kim and Kim easily pushed their lead to three before taking the win. Si Woo's birdie at the 14th was from distance, too, and banked in perfectly.

Tom nearly had a hole-in-one at the 16th and actually banked his ball off the flag stick. That would have been the third ace in Presidents Cup history.

Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune, meanwhile, took off on the back nine to grab their 3&1 win. After hanging in a battle on the front nine, the pair won back-to-back holes before making the turn to take control of the match while Xander Schauffele and Cameron Young struggled to get putts to fall. Eventually, after Young missed a birdie look at the 17th, Matsuyama and Hisatsune were able to put the Internationals on the board for the first time all day.

The two teams will return to Medinah on Friday for five foursomes, or alternate shot, matches.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: US edge opening session against International team
articles.summary: The US begin their bid to win an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup by opening up a 3-2 lead over the International team on day one.
articles.body:
The United States began their bid to win an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup by opening up a 3-2 lead over the International team at the end of Thursday's fourballs matches at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.

Justin Thomas and rookie Jackson Koivun put the first point on the board for Brandt Snedeker's American team with a resounding 4&3 win over Canada's Corey Conners and Colombia's Nico Echavarria.

World number one Scottie Scheffler, who was partnered with his long-time friend Sam Burns, took the 17th hole and held on to close out their victory over Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, who were left to rue several missed putts down the stretch.

And two-time major champions Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa ensured the US would take an advantage into Friday's five foursome matches.

Clark and Morikawa led from the opening hole against Australia's Adam Scott and reigning Open champion Ryan Fox before completing their 3&2 success with two holes to spare.

"A session win is a session win; we're going to take it any way we can get it," said Snedeker.

However, Geoff Ogilvy's International side will head into the alternate shot format on Friday with optimism of remaining in contention to claim only their second ever triumph in the biennial contest, some 28 years after their first in 1998.

Japanese duo Hideki Matsuyama and debutant Ryo Hisatsune recorded a 3&1 success over Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele, while Kim Si-woo and Tom Kim always looked comfortable in their 3&2 win over Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay.

The five foursome matches scheduled to take place on Friday will be followed by two sessions on Saturday, split between four four-ball matches in the morning and four foursomes in the afternoon.

All 12 players on each team will then compete in the singles matches on Sunday, with 15½ points required for overall victory.

articles.title: Presidents Cup: Team USA lead International Team 3-2 after Thursday fourballs as Scottie Scheffler makes winning start
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns defeated Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im in a final-hole thriller; Team USA won three of the five fourballs matches to take a narrow lead over the International Team on the opening day; watch day two live on Friday from 7pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Brandt Snedeker's side have historically dominated the biennial contest but were presented with a tough test on the opening day at Medinah Country Club, where the Internationals won two of the five points on offer.

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler ended his winless record alongside Sam Burns by edging a final-hole thriller against Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, following Justin Thomas partnering rookie Jackson Koivun to a 4&3 win over Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria.

The all-Japanese pairing of Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune despatched Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele 3&1, before Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa beat Ryan Fox and Adam Scott 3&2 to ensure Team USA would win the session.

The United States have led after the opening day in nine of the last 10 Presidents Cups, although Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim reduced their advantage by seeing off Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay 3&2 in the bottom match.

How Team USA edged ahead after fourballs

A high-scoring top match saw Scheffler win the first with a 15-foot birdie, before Burns holed from 10 feet to match Lee's monster putt from off the green. Both teams then birdied the next two holes.

Im won the fifth with a birdie, while both teams made two on the par-three ninth, with Burns rolling in from nearly 20 feet after Lee had fired his tee shot close. The Internationals then squandered several chances to move ahead.

They eventually took the lead when Im converted a 10-foot birdie at the 13th, but Burns immediately responded with a close-range birdie at the next. The teams remained tied until both Internationals bogeyed the 17th, handing the hole to Team USA.

Scheffler then splashed out of the greenside bunker at the par-four last to within inches of the hole, securing the par and sealing a first win together for him and Burns at either the Presidents Cup or Ryder Cup.

"We just did our best to stay in it," Scheffler said. "I felt like both teams got off to pretty hot starts today and we cooled off a little bit off that. Sam [Burns] hit probably the shot of the match there on 14.

"We lost 13 to go one down and then he hit one in there to a couple feet. I felt like that was really a big moment for us as a team, and he stepped up when we needed him to."

Thomas extended his perfect Presidents Cup fourballs record with an impressive partnership alongside 21-year-old rookie Koivun, with the American pair never trailing as they secured the first point of this year's contest.

The pair won three holes in a four-hole stretch from the third before Conners claimed the seventh, with the gap remaining at two until Thomas closed out a seventh consecutive fourballs victory by birdieing the 14th and 15th.

"It was fun to be out there with him and doing his thing," Thomas said. "He's really impressive to watch and I'm really happy he's on my team. It was cool to watch him do his thing out there and show up in some pretty big moments."

Fox and Scott trailed from the first hole in their defeat by Clark and Morikawa, while Matsuyama and Hisatsune fought back after falling behind early to beat Young and Schauffele.

"I saw a lot of good golf out there," International captain Geoff Ogilvy said. "We had a couple of really good solid matches there and we had a match go up to 18, which would have been nice if it went the other way, but we'll take that (3-2)."

In the bottom match, Kim and Kim squandered an early two-hole lead before restoring control with back-to-back wins from the 13th. Gotterup kept the match alive with a long-range par at the 15th, but Tom Kim sent his tee shot to tap-in range at the next to close out another point for the Internationals.

Snedeker 'proud' after Team USA grab early lead

Team USA require a further 12 points to retain the trophy or 12.5 more points to extend their winning streak over the International Team, with 25 more points on offer - including five in Friday foursomes session.

"I saw those guys [Team USA] competing their asses off out there," United States captain Snedeker said. "I'm really proud of them. A session win is a session win - we're going to take it any way we can get it.

"So happy for Scottie [Scheffler] and Sam [Burns] to go out there in that lead match and get that big win for us to lead us off. This is a long week and this is one session. We've got four more to go, but just proud of the way these guys started us off.

articles.title: Presidents Cup Day 1 winners, losers: Justin Thomas shines for US team
articles.summary: Justin Thomas, Wyndham Clark and Xander Schauffele are among the biggest winners and losers after Day 1 at the 2026 Presidents Cup.
articles.body:
MEDINAH, IL — Actor and longtime Chicago sports fan Bill Murray carried the Presidents Cup out to its pedestal. Jim Cornelison, the legendary singer known to Chicagoans for his thunderous rendition of the "Star-Spangled Banner" at Chicago Blackhawks games, belted out the National Anthem. Military choppers flew overhead as he reached the crescendo. Thousands packed into the stadium-style seating around the first tee at Medinah Country Club roared.

But the rest of Day 1 at the 2026 Presidents Cup proved to be a more restrained experience for the American crowd as the U.S. and International teams went back-and-forth during the first session of matches.

The U.S. grabbed a 3-2 lead when four-ball action was complete on Thursday, Sept. 24, as stars Scottie Scheffler , Justin Thomas and Wyndham Clark were each part of pairings that secured a point. But the Internationals proved resilient playing in front of a revved-up crowd sporting red, white and blue.

Here are the winners and losers from Day 1 at the 2026 Presidents Cup:

Presidents Cup opens with pivotal Day 1 matches at Medinah

Thomas has been the most reliable match-play golfer for the U.S. in these team events for a decade now, and Thursday only served as further confirmation of that status. Paired alongside 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun , Thomas was the steady veteran as the U.S. secured its first point of the Presidents Cup with a 4&3 win over Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria. Thomas was the best on the course off the tee, and nobody gained more strokes on the field during Day 1. Thomas has now won seven consecutive four-ball matches in international team competition.

The most competitive match during Day 1 was the first one as Burns and Scheffler went all the way to No. 18 for a 1 up win over Sungjae Im and Min Woo Lee. It was Burns, though, who contributed what Scheffler later declared, "the shot of the match." After the International team took its first lead with a birdie by Im on No. 13, Burns fired his approach shot on the 14th hole to within three feet of the cup to set up a birdie to tie the match once more. This was the first win in five tries for Burns when paired with his good friend and Scheffler, the world's No. 1 golfer, at either the Ryder Cup or Presidents Cup.

Clark and Collin Morikawa coasted to a 3&2 win over Ryan Fox and Adam Scott by racing out to an early lead. The Americans had three birdies on the first four holes and a 3-up lead by the end of the sixth hole. Clark's hot putter proved to be a difference maker as he gained more than two strokes putting when compared to everyone else playing at Medinah during Thursday's four-ball matches.

Matsuyama entered this Presidents Cup as one of the longest-tenured members of the International team, but he hasn't had much success in team golf over the years. On Thursday, he formed a strong combination with fellow Japanese golfer and Presidents Cup rookie Ryo Hisatsune. They grabbed control of their match against Xander Schauffele and Cameron Young, and Matsuyama's pure approach shots and timely putts kept his team rolling after the Internationals came back from an early deficit.

Tom Kim played well with Si Woo Kim for the International team two years ago at the Presidents Cup, and they picked up where they left off in the final match of Day 1. Tom Kim was the best golfer on the course for the Internationals in terms of strokes gained. He did his best work around the green, finishing with five birdies, but he was also top-five in the field in terms of strokes gained tee-to-green. Thursday further solidified Tom Kim's spot as one of the most dangerous match-play opponents the Internationals can turn to over the final three days at Medinah.

Schauffele and Young couldn't muster much as a tandem on Thursday, but it was Schauffele's poor play that stood out. He was among the worst golfers on the course around the green and tee-to-green. How much U.S. team captain Brandt Snedeker relies on Schauffele the rest of the event bears watching. He's among the most decorated Americans playing at Medinah this week, but he has just one top-10 finish since June. This performance on Thursday was more reminiscent of that recent form than his past history of success at these international events.

Lee and Im nearly pulled off a huge upset over Scheffler and Burns to start the Presidents Cup because Sungjae Im was the best player on course tee-to-green by a wide margin. But he missed some key putts, and Lee didn't hold up his end of the bargain, wasting a performance in which Im out-dueled the world's best golfer. Lee was the worst putter at Medinah on Thursday and those missed chances wound up costing him and Im by the end of the match.

The 2026 British Open champion struggled in his first Presidents Cup appearance partnered with Adam Scott, and the duo got waxed by Clark and Morikawa. Fox lost nearly two strokes on the field with his driver and iron play out of whack. Fox doesn't have a top-25 finish since winning the Claret Jug in July, and Thursday was not a promising indication that he's returned to top form.

Other than Koivun, Cantlay was the lowest-ranked captain's pick this year based on Presidents Cup points. His selection was largely because of his track record for the U.S. in international team competition, where he's 10-4 in Presidents Cup matches and 6-5-2 in the Ryder Cup. But playing with Presidents Cup rookie Chris Gotterup, Cantlay could not replicate his past success on Thursday. Gotterup was the worst American golfer on the course during Day 1 based on strokes gained, and Cantlay was unable to pick him up after failing to hit the timely putts he has connected on in the past. His putting stroke was an issue throughout this season and it could be a problem this weekend.

Wyndham Clark called the crowd "kind of dead out there" and noted he and his teammates "weren't really feeling the fans as much as normal" on Thursday. Snedeker described the atmosphere as "weird" after the boisterous scene at the first tee to start Day 1. Clark said he brought it up as a way to challenge fans to be louder for the final three days of competition.

The Presidents Cup continues Friday, September 25 with the first set of foursomes matches at Medinah Country Club. The U.S. currently leads the Internationals, 3-2. Here's the full list of matchups, tee times and how to watch.

Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns are riding high off their first win together at either a Presidents Cup or Ryder Cup. That momentum led U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker to pair them together again, this time against Corey Conners and Cup rookie Nick Taylor.

Another rookie, American Jackson Koivun, will sit out Friday's matches after winning his first point alongside Justin Thomas on Thursday. Thomas will be paired with Cameron Young on Friday, and the duo will face Adam Scott and Christiaan Bezuidenhout.

The final foursomes match of the day is sure to bring the fireworks as Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim – fresh off a 3 and 2 win over Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay on Thursday – will face Cantlay and Xander Schauffele. This is the third time these four have faced off at a Presidents Cup. In 2022, the Kims beat Cantlay and Schauffele 1 up in Saturday afternoon fourballs. The Americans got their revenge in 2024 though, when Cantlay and Schauffele beat the Kims 1 up in Saturday afternoon foursomes.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson runs wild as Falcons trounce Packers 35-14
articles.summary: Bijan Robinson rushed for 194 yards and two touchdowns as the Atlanta Falcons capitalized on the return of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and trounced the pun...
articles.body:
Bijan Robinson rushed for 194 yards and two touchdowns as the Atlanta Falcons capitalized on the return of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and trounced the punchless Green Bay Packers 35-14 on Thursday night.

Atlanta (1-2) erased an early 7-0 deficit by scoring 27 straight points to take control amid a chorus of boos at Lambeau Field. The Falcons outrushed the Packers 242 yards to 17.

Green Bay (1-2) lost a home opener for the first time since falling 30-22 to the San Francisco 49ers in 2012. The Packers had won 13 straight home openers from 2013-25 to share the NFL record with the Miami Dolphins , who also won 13 in a row from 1976-88.

Penix went 18 of 25 for 256 yards with one touchdown and an interception in his first action since tearing the ACL in his left knee during a loss to Carolina on Nov. 16. Atlanta (1-2) had struggled to produce any offense whatsoever with Cooper Rush starting at quarterback the first two weeks of the season.

Robinson and Drake London became the first teammates to each compile at least 150 yards from scrimmage against the Packers at Lambeau Field. London caught nine passes for 194 yards.

Green Bay's Jordan Love went 28 of 53 for 312 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson combined for 17 yards on eight carries.

Love was working behind an offensive line missing left guard Aaron Banks and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, who tore his patellar tendon Sunday and will miss the rest of the season. Banks was dealing with a toe injury.

Jager Burton, a rookie fifth-round pick from Kentucky, made his first career start at left guard, and 2025 second-round selection Anthony Belton started at right tackle.

The lack of discipline that hindered Green Bay in its first two games cropped up again Thursday.

Green Bay led 7-0 and had forced an apparent third-and-11 incompletion late in the first quarter when Brenton Cox Jr. was called for roughing the passer. Robinson delivered a 55-yard carry on the next play to set up his own 3-yard touchdown run.

The Packers had committed an NFL-high 26 penalties through the first two weeks of the season.

Robinson long run allowed Atlanta to take a snap inside an opponent's 20-yard line for the first time this season. Atlanta had been the first team since the 2008 Rams not to run any plays in the red zone through the first two weeks of a season.

Atlanta dominated the rest of the first half and led 17-7 at the break.

Nick Folk put Atlanta ahead by hitting a 44-yard field goal with 4:48 left in the second quarter. After Atlanta's Zach Harrison blocked Trey Smack's 47-yard field-goal attempt, Penix threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to Austin Hooper on third-and-goal with 59 seconds left in the half.

Green Bay wasted a red-zone opportunity on its first drive of the second half when Love couldn't connect with Christian Watson in the end zone on fourth-and-1 from the 7. Atlanta extended the lead to 24-7 on its next possession, as Brian Robinson 's 7-yard touchdown run capped a 10-play, 92-yard drive.

Folk added a 31-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter before Love threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden with 8:18 remaining. Bijan Robinson capped the scoring with a 2-yard TD.

Falcons: CB A.J. Terrell (groin) didn't play after getting placed on injured reserve this week.

Packers: LB Edgerrin Cooper was evaluated for a concussion in the second half. G Jacob Monk hurt his quadriceps late in the fourth quarter.

Falcons: At New Orleans on Monday, Oct. 5.

articles.title: Endangered dormice on Babers Farm signal healthy landscape
articles.summary: Dormice are detected on a farm near Bridport during surveys by the Countryside Regeneration Trust.
articles.body:
Endangered dormice have been found on a farm that has been working to improve biodiversity and nature habitats.

Babers Farm in Marshwood, near Bridport, Dorset, is under the stewardship of the Countryside Regeneration Trust (CRT), which seeks to create nature-friendly farms.

Hazel dormice are a European Protected Species and are considered vulnerable to extinction, but their presence is a marker of a healthy, well-connected landscape.

Since it began surveys in May, the CRT has installed 39 footprint tunnels along hedgerows and woodland edges, with nine of the tunnels recording dormouse footprints.

Babers is one of the first CRT farms to return positive dormouse results after a fundraising appeal to fund surveys and habitat improvements across its 16 properties.

The survival of dormice is dependent on diverse woodland, species-rich hedgerows and connected habitats that provide year-round food and shelter.

CRT conservation officer Ruth Moss said: "It's really encouraging to see evidence of hazel dormouse presence on the farm.

"As the survey progresses, the results will build up a more complete picture of where, within the areas surveyed, dormice are present on the farm.

"Having a current set of data helps us to manage these areas with dormice in mind."

The CRT works with tenant farmers to restore soil health, improve biodiversity and strengthen the natural ecosystem while producing food.

Footprint tunnels have also been installed at Bere Marsh Farm in Dorset and at Pierrepont Farm and Green Farm in Surrey.

The surveys will continue in Dorset throughout September and into November in Surrey.

Dormice have also been detected at Turnastone Court Farm and Awnells Farm in Herefordshire.

CRT supporters raised £6,000 to fund dormouse surveys and habitat improvements across the charity's farms.

As surveying continues through 2026, the CRT hopes to build a clearer picture of dormouse populations across its farms and use the findings to guide future habitat management.

The tiny nocturnal species has disappeared from 20 counties in England since the 19th Century.

The loss of traditional skills such as coppicing has led to their habitats being lost, which also makes it more difficult for populations to travel between locations.

Climate change has also disrupted their hibernation patterns.

articles.title: NFL media, Packers fans sound off after dismal loss in home opener
articles.summary: NFL media and Packers fans were plenty willing to throw around the blame after suffering through Green Bay's miserable performance on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Opening night at Lambeau Field for the 2026 Green Bay Packers was anything but grand. Though the home team took an early lead, it certainly became a performance that turned dark quickly.

While the wounded offensive line continued to have problems protecting quarterback Jordan Love during an embarrassing 35-14 loss to the previously 0-2 Atlanta Falcons , the defense finished the night allowing nearly 500 total yards.

And while Falcons running back Bijan Robinson led a punishing ground game that netted Atlanta 242 yards, the Packers managed just 17 yards on nine carries. On four of six possessions in the first half, the Packers did not get a first down.

Those are just a couple of the many problems the Packers had trouble solving Sept. 24. Love threw for 312 yards, but he missed some throws, his timing was off due to Atlanta's pressure and he never got into sync with his receivers.

Meanwhile, the Packers' secondary couldn't keep Falcons receiver Drake London from having a spectacular night. He finished with 9 catches for 184 yards and a touchdown. Many of the receptions were chunk plays as he averaged 21.5 yards a catch.

And to add to the insult, Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. threw for 256 yards, though he hadn't played a game since last November because of a torn ACL

Both NFL media and Packers fans were plenty willing to throw around the blame after suffering through the brutal rout.

articles.title: Falcons news: Why did Kevin Stefanski go for 2 after final touchdown?
articles.summary: Kevin Stefanski had no interest in leaving anything to chance. Leading the Green Bay Packers 33-14 late in the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field, the Atlanta...
articles.body:
Kevin Stefanski had no interest in leaving anything to chance. Leading the Green Bay Packers 33-14 late in the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field , the Atlanta Falcons head coach made an eye-catching decision. This was after Bijan Robinson scored his second touchdown of the night. Instead of sending out the kicking unit for the extra point, Stefanski kept his offense on the field. They attempted a two-point conversion. The decision immediately raised questions , but Stefanski's reasoning was straightforward: Jordan Love and Green Bay 's explosive passing attack demanded a three-touchdown cushion.

"It's the math. I look across the field, and I see Jordan Love and that passing attack and I want to make sure we're at 21 (point lead)," Stefanski explained after the game.

The calculation was simple. A successful conversion would turn Atlanta's 19-point advantage into 21. This meant Green Bay would need three touchdowns to erase the deficit. Had the Falcons kicked the extra point, they would have led by 20, leaving more unconventional comeback paths available. Stefanski's gamble worked, with Atlanta converting to make it 35–14 and effectively ending any realistic comeback hopes.

The victory also represented a major milestone for Stefanski in his first season leading Atlanta. He spent 14 seasons with Minnesota before taking over Cleveland in 2020, where he won two AP NFL Coach of the Year awards and guided the Browns to playoff appearances in 2020 and 2023. Known for his wide-zone rushing concepts, play-action passing and analytical approach, Stefanski entered Atlanta with a reputation for calculated decision-making. Against Green Bay, that philosophy was on full display.

articles.body: Andrea Revuelta y Paula Martín, ambas de 20 años, son dos golfistas amateur españolas que están haciendo historia. Actualmente ocupan el primer y segundo puesto del ranking mundial amateur femenino (WAGR) respectivamente, aunque semanas atrás las posiciones llegaron a estar invertidas entre ellas. Las dos son madrileñas, Andrea miembro del Real Sociedad Hípica Española y Paula del Real Club de Golf La Herrería. Revuelta tiene como entrenador a Alejandro Ramos y Martín a Alejandro Larrazábal, si bien los dos diamantes en bruto del golf nacional tienen en común la cantidad de horas que han pasado preparándose en el Centro de Tecnificación de la Federación de Golf de Madrid (CETEMA), así como en las concentraciones de los equipos nacionales de la Real Federación Española de Golf. A día de hoy incluso comparten equipo en la Universidad de Stanford, donde esta temporada se proclamaron campeonas nacionales. Freddy Lilly, director técnico de la RFGM, recalca que forjar a jugadas de este nivel es un trabajo en equipo, aunque reconoce que Andrea y Paula siempre han destacado. “Ya desde pequeñas apuntaban maneras, han tenido grandes profesores, y eso se nota. Cuando entraron en el programa CETEMA, nuestra función fue que siguieran creciendo como jugadoras y como personas. Enseñarles a desenvolverse por sí solas y a tener un plan de entrenamiento estructurado y bien planificado, que les sirva para cuando dieran el salto a la universidad”, explica Lilly. “Su evolución ha sido muy buena estos últimos años. Tanto Alejandro Larrazábal con Paula como Alejandro Ramos con Andrea están haciendo una gran labor para que todo esto esté sucediendo”, destaca el preparador de la RFGM. El responsable de la madrileña pone en valor también la manera en que se está empujando esta nueva generación femenina: “Han coincidido con dos grandes jugadoras como Cayetana Fernández y Paula de Francisco, y se han ido retroalimentando unas a otras”. Actualmente, las cuatro mejores amateur españolas han pasado por el CETEMA. En este sentido, Lilly apunta: “También ha habido años de sequía, pero aquí no sólo formamos golfistas, también personas. En el caso de Paula y Andrea, que han conseguido entrar en Stanford, además de buenas jugadoras son brillantes estudiantes”. Freddy apunta además: “Estar ahí arriba no es casualidad para dos jugadoras cuyo valor principal es la disciplina y el orden. Con esas dos cosas, más talento y entrenamiento se puede llegar al número 1”. En la misma línea analiza Marcelo Prieto, técnicos de la RFEG especializado en golf femenino, a las dos talentosas jugadoras. “Técnicamente son muy buenas, son jugadoras que toman muy buenas decisiones. Ya de pequeñas tomaban muy buenas decisiones en el campo. Eran muy completas en todos los golpes y muy consistentes. Tenían distancia y eran jugadoras de mucho talento. Tienen mucho talento, pero detrás hay mucho trabajo", subraya. Sobre el nivel actual de las dos amateur españolas, indica: “Tanto Andrea como Paula están ahí. Están demostrando que tienen nivel para ganar en cualquier momento". Cabe recordar que Paula Martín ya fue octava en el British femenino absoluto en 2025 –clasificada tras ganar en modalidad amateur- y este año terminó 29ª; por su parte, Andrea ha peleado por el Open de España y en su categoría fue segunda en Augusta este curso. Prieto nos recuerda una anécdota sobre Paula Martín durante un campeonato: "Me decía: 'Mira, son mis compañeras de Stanford, la número uno del mundo, la número dos'. Y al final, tres años después, ella ya está ahí. Creo que ha hecho y está haciendo mejor papel que cualquier jugadora que ha pasado por esa universidad". Sobre esta misma jugadora, Marcelo confiesa: “No tiene ninguna deficiencia en ningún apartado de su juego. Es una jugadora muy natural. Ve el golpe y lo ejecuta". Centrados en Andrea Revuelta, admite: “Técnicamente, para mí es excelente. Cuando tiene la posibilidad de ganar, sabe ganar”. En este sentido, matiza: “Las dos, cuando se ha presentado la oportunidad, han sabido ganar”. Otra cosa que explica el técnico tiene que ver con el nivel de trabajo de las dos jóvenes: “El deporte de élite es muy exigente. Tienen que sacrificar mucho por el deporte, pero luego también obtienen sus recompensas”. Una de ellas, recalar en la prestigiosa Stanford: “La universidad americana ha sido el trampolín para subir y tener la posibilidad de competir a un nivel muy alto", señala Marcelo. Alejandro Ramos, que entrena a Andrea Revuelta desde hace años, destaca la fortaleza mental de su pupila. "En ciertas situaciones donde los demás se frustran antes y lo dejan, ella, aunque se frustre, continúa y lo sigue intentando. Cuando no gana un campeonato, a los 30 minutos está muy motivada por seguir mejorando”, dice. Sin duda esto habla de Revuelta como una jugadora que ha madurado y que reúne todos los ingredientes para ser profesional en caso de dar el salto. Su capacidad de sacrificio, queda patente a tenor de las palabras de su entrenador: “Es una persona que tiene la capacidad de comprometerse con lo que se ha propuesto, tanto entrenando como compitiendo. Eso lo hace por encima de lo que siente o de lo que le apetece". Para Alejandro, parte del éxito de Andrea radica en que “tiene bastante fe en el proceso". Eso sí, es pronto para hablar del profesionalismo: “Ella va año a año porque así da su mejor versión”, indica Ramos. En cualquier caso, explica Alejandro Ramos, "en momentos muy especiales, Andrea rinde muy alto. Cuanta más presión había, mejor jugaba”. Respecto a que sea la número 1 del ranking amateur, confiesa que cuando Andrea ingresó en Stanford no es algo que se imaginaran: “No es algo en lo que pensábamos”. En resumen, Ramos analiza así a su jugadora: "Lo que Andrea tiene diferente es que posee habilidad, posee esa base, pero tiene una fortaleza mental que le permite seguir en cualquier situación, aun cuando las cosas no salen bien”. Aunque son incontables horas de trabajo, el preparador considera que sobresale la personalidad de Revuelta: "Le mete corazón a las cosas que hace. No las hace por hacer; le mete mucha pasión e ilusión". Anne Walker, directora de Golf Femenino en la Universidad de Stanford desde 2012, también comparte con MARCA algunas de sus impresiones sobre Andrea y Paula. Bajo su dirección, las dos han ganado este año el título nacional. Sobre las fortalezas de sus jugadoras, Walker apunta: “Ambas son competidoras experimentadas y cuentan con una trayectoria impresionante. Paula es una luchadora que nunca se rinde; ¡es capaz de meter la bola en el hoyo con la mente y de ejecutar golpes increíbles cuando la mayoría pensaría que no hay opción alguna! Es una gran especialista en el putt y una trabajadora incansable”. Sobre Andrea, detalla: “Es una competidora paciente, serena y tranquila. Tiene un fuego interior, pero por fuera no se deja afectar emocionalmente en exceso por ningún resultado concreto. Posee un toque cerca del green y con los hierros que recuerdan al inolvidable Seve Ballesteros”. En relación a la evolución de las dos madrileñas con el equipo de Stanford y su aportación al mismo, la directora que ha llevado al conjunto femenino a ganar cuatro campeonatos (2015, 2022, 2024, 2026), comenta: “Ambas han madurado y ganado independencia en Stanford. Sienten un amor por el golf —y específicamente por el golf de equipo— que resulta contagioso y fomenta una cultura maravillosa en nuestro vestuario. Tienen una perspectiva global y aportan humildad y gratitud al ambiente del equipo. Hemos tenido mucha suerte de contar con su liderazgo; han influido enormemente en nuestros éxitos”, declara. Anne Walker reconoce que desde el primer momento supo que trabajaba con muy buenos mimbres cuando le preguntamos si creía que Paula y Andrea, cuando llegaron a Stanford, se podrían algún día convertir en primeras del ranking amateur. “¡Sí! Ambas cuentan con un apoyo increíble en España, con una excelente formación, enseñanza y experiencia en el equipo nacional. Gracias al acceso a nuestras instalaciones de práctica y a la competición de alto nivel durante todo el año, su sólida base les permitió destacar y progresar enormemente”, explica. A estas alturas parece claro que las dos protagonistas de este reportaje están listas para dar el paso a profesional si lo desean. En este sentido, Walker comenta: “Creo que su etapa en EE.UU. les será de gran utilidad cuando den el salto al profesionalismo. Han hecho muchas amistades aquí y se han acostumbrado a las distintas microculturas del país. Conocen bien a las jugadoras contra las que competirán en el siguiente nivel, lo que les dará confianza en su capacidad para competir en cualquier categoría. Además, siempre podrán volver a Stanford como base y utilizar nuestras instalaciones de práctica y centros de entrenamiento, lo que facilitará enormemente su vida como profesionales”.

articles.title: Falcons Get Revealing Kevin Stefanski-Michael Penix Report After Packers Win
articles.summary: Kevin Stefanski reportedly shared a telling Michael Penix Jr. belief inside the Falcons' building before Atlanta broke through in Green Bay. The post Falcons...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons needed something to change after an 0-2 start that featured just 16 points and zero red-zone snaps.

Kevin Stefanski apparently believed Michael Penix Jr. could be the answer.

Penix made his 2026 debut Thursday night at Lambeau Field and helped Atlanta produce by far its best offensive performance of the young season, beating the Green Bay Packers 35-14. Afterward, a new report revealed just how strongly Stefanski believed Penix could bring together what the Falcons had been building behind the scenes.

Kevin Stefanski Had Strong Michael Penix Jr. Belief Before Win

The confidence wasn't something Stefanski only expressed after watching Penix lead Atlanta to its first win.

NFL insider Josina Anderson reported that Stefanski had been telling people inside the Falcons' building what he expected from Penix before Thursday night's game.

"Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski was heard telling folks in the building he felt like Michael Penix was going to "pull everything together" they've been working on leading into tonight's game vs the Packers, per league source. This was a very important victory for Stefanski—particularly since he discussed how he felt like he could improve Penix in his interview with Atlanta, the source repeatedly said."

Penix didn't start perfectly. His third pass of the night was intercepted by Xavier McKinney , and Atlanta came away empty on its opening possession.

Penix completed 18 of 25 passes for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He connected with Austin Hooper for a 5-yard touchdown late in the second quarter and also converted a two-point attempt in the fourth.

Atlanta finished with 498 total yards after managing 499 combined yards over its first two games.

The Falcons also rushed for 244 yards. Bijan Robinson accounted for 194 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries, while Drake London caught nine passes for 194 yards.

Michael Penix Jr. Helps Deliver Stefanski's First Falcons Win

The performance looked nothing like the offense Atlanta put on the field during its first two games.

Cooper Rush started losses to the Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers while Penix continued working back from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season. Atlanta scored 13 points in Week 1 and only three in Week 2, with Rush committing five turnovers across the two games.

Penix's return changed the offense immediately, even with the early interception.

Atlanta scored on five of its next six meaningful possessions after the turnover, building a 24-7 advantage by late in the third quarter. The Falcons controlled the ball for more than 37 minutes and ran 41 times compared with only nine rushing attempts for Green Bay.

"Tommy (Rees) did a great job of giving him some concepts that he's really comfortable with. And then, you know, Mike made great decisions with the ball," Stefanski said, per SI's Darius Hayes .

The win carried added weight for both Stefanski and Penix.

Stefanski arrived in Atlanta after the Falcons fired Raheem Morris and was hired in part to fix an offense that had struggled to find stability at quarterback. According to Anderson's source, improving Penix was specifically part of the case Stefanski made during his interview for the job.

Thursday was the first real look at what that partnership might become.

One game won't settle whether Penix is Atlanta's long-term answer. But after two weeks in which almost nothing worked offensively, his return produced 35 points, nearly 500 yards and Stefanski's first Falcons victory.

For one night, what Stefanski thought Penix could pull together looked a lot more tangible.

articles.title: Victims 'grossly failed' by Zafer Dogan bail decision
articles.summary: Victims of Zafer Dogan were living close to the 32-year-old who took thousands of pictures of children at a playground from his bedroom window.
articles.body:
Victims and their families were "grossly failed" by the court system that bailed a sex offender and repeatedly allowed him to return to his home overlooking the playground he targeted, London's victims' commissioner said.

Zafer Dogan, 32, of Enfield, north London, was jailed on Thursday for two years and four months for taking thousands of pictures of children and using AI software to "nudify" them.

Andrea Simon said the case showed "the justice system did not centre victims" and called for a multi-agency review.

The Ministry of Justice said while the Crown Prosecution Service had the right to challenge them, final bail decisions were "made by the independent judiciary".

The ministry added: "The protection of victims, witnesses, and the public must always be considered when deciding whether or not an offender should be released on bail."

Dogan had pleaded guilty to three counts of making indecent images of a child, which included 900 category C images, 294 category B images and 653 category A images, which are the most serious.

He also admitted possessing extreme pornography, possessing a prohibited image of a child, creating purported intimate images of an adult, obstructing a constable in the execution of their duty and a further two counts of making indecent photographs of a child.

According to the police, he had taken more than 5,000 pictures, many from his bedroom window.

Despite protests from the police and prosecutors, he had previously been bailed back to his flat, forcing one family who had fallen victim to his crimes to move into temporary accommodation.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today , Simon said: "I think victims and their families were grossly failed by the decision to allow this paedophile to return to an address where he was overlooking a playground near to his victims.

"The case [shows that] the justice system just does not centre victims. To know that the police and prosecutors opposed bail multiple times, but nevertheless, he was returned to the community, is an indication that the capacity pressures on prisons are not being balanced with the impacts that that's having on victims' lives.

"We seem to be lurching from one crisis to another, and victim safety and their rights seem to be put to one side, as the justice system struggles."

Simon's criticism was echoed by Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley who said it was "unfathomable" that Dogan was ever granted bail.

Sir Mark said: "Prosecutors rightly opposed bail on multiple occasions, building on officers' clear assessments of the great risk he posed, and yet bail decisions were ultimately made that prioritised the offender's interests over the safety and the peace of mind of the victims."

Former Tory justice secretary Sir Robert Buckland told the BBC's The World At One : "Until justice is given the same priority that we give to health and education, this problem will recur.

"Dangerous men should not be released on bail when they are clearly going to go on and commit further offences."

Sir Tom Winsor, former Her Majesty's Chief Inspector of Constabulary, told the programme: "Judges appear to be taking prison capacity into account.

"The result is prolific offenders are being bailed. Releasing dangerous people into the community is an extremely serious thing.

"Of course we have an independent judiciary but their obligation is to also explain their decisions."

Remand and bail decisions are made by independent judges or magistrates.

According to the prosecutor, Dogan had been on conditional bail "throughout" the proceedings:

16 July 2026: Dogan was arrested on suspicion of offences involving indecent images of children

4 August: He was arrested again and the following day was charged and remanded by police

6 August: Dogan's first appearance at Highbury Corner Magistrates' Court where he pleaded guilty to all offences. He was granted conditional bail

7 August: A bail hearing was held at Wood Green Crown Court. The court decided bail conditions would remain with an additional one for Dogan to attend appointment with probation for pre-sentence report

7 September: Bail hearing at Wood Green Crown Court at request of Police and Crown Prosecution Service. Judge brought forward sentencing in an attempt to mitigate

11 September: Snaresbrook Crown Court sentencing - judge sends back to Wood Green Crown Court on 23 September

23 September: Wood Green Crown Court sentencing adjourned

24 September: Sentenced at Wood Green Crown Court

Simon said there were parallels to be drawn with the case of serial sex offender and murderer Simon Levy.

Levy killed two women and raped a third in 2025 while on bail for other offences, after a series of decisions by authorities that left him free to roam the streets.

Levy had been reported to the Metropolitan Police for a sexual assault in 2017. He then assaulted two women in 2018, but was only convicted for those offences in 2021.

After being released from prison - where he sexually assaulted a female officer - he committed other assaults before the 2025 murders.

Sir Mark previously described that case as a "whole system failing", criticising the decision of the courts and Crown Prosecution Service to bail Levy, while also apologising for the Met's own failings in the case.

Levy is a registered sex offender and was being monitored by police at the time of the attacks.

The force failed to treat the first murder as such until after the second murder and released Levy on bail leaving him free to kill.

It also failed to fully pursue a rape investigation and closed the case, meaning Levy went on to kill Sheryl Wilkins in the same place where he had attacked the surviving rape victim.

Two Met police officers are currently under investigation by the police watchdog for downgrading Levy's risk to women - a decision that was not reversed even after police knew he was attacking women again.

London's victims' commissioner Simon also raised concerns over the government's early release scheme which is set to see about 2,550 eligible offenders leaving jails in England and Wales by the end of the year.

"I hear from victims about what they think they want to do ahead of offenders' early releases from prison," she said.

"They feel they may have to install security cameras or change their daily routines, or live in fear."

articles.title: Matt LaFleur demands a “Long, Hard Look” after the Green Bay Packers’ humbling loss to Falcons
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers are facing a level of adversity that has become difficult to ignore. After decades of sustained competitiveness, Green Bay now finds it...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are facing a level of adversity that has become difficult to ignore. After decades of sustained competitiveness, Green Bay now finds itself sitting at 1-2 and could easily have started the season without a win had the New York Jets held onto their late lead.

A growing injury list has only added to the team's problems, but the collapse against Atlanta still came as a shock to Packers fans. Instead of celebrating a strong home opener, the Green and Gold watched their team get overwhelmed at Lambeau Field, ending Thursday night with a painful 35-14 defeat and a season that suddenly feels like it has hit its lowest point.

Matt LaFleur on the Packers loss to the Falcons

Matt LaFleur and the Packers now must regroup, reassess its problems, and find a way back to winning football.

"Well, that was a humbling night. Certainly, I don't think anybody is pleased about this. We've got a couple extra days here, and everybody has to take a long, hard look at ourselves," commented the Packers head coach via NFL insider Ryan Wood.

The Packers cannot simply replace Micah Parsons ' All Pro impact, erase the loss of Zach Bako-Bewele, or immediately solve the uncertainty surrounding Josh Jacobs . Some issues may linger throughout 2026, but Green Bay 's latest showing cannot be excused.

Jordan Love struggled to make the most of crucial opportunities , with several questionable decisions preventing Green Bay from building momentum. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson still gave the Packers some production, combining for 196 receiving yards and two touchdowns, but their efforts were largely overshadowed by uneven quarterback play and a ground attack that generated almost nothing.

Matt LaFleur will need to make changes quickly and rally his team before Green Bay travels to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next Sunday.

articles.title: Drake London teams with Michael Penix in season-saving win for Falcons
articles.summary: The Falcons' offense found its rhythm on Thursday Night Football due to Drake London reuniting with Michael Penix
articles.body:
All it took was the return of Michael Penix Jr. for former Trojan Drake London to show what type of receiver he can be. It was a long two weeks for London in September, dealing with substandard quarterback play with the Atlanta Falcons . To be fair, he hasn't had competent quarterback play his whole tenure in Atlanta. However, there was some magic on display in the connection between Penix and London on Thursday Night Football.

The Green Bay Packers were on the wrong side of that reality. London posted a nearly perfect performance. London hauled in 9 of his 10 targets for 194 yards. That is double what he had combined in the first two weeks of the season. The impact of Penix was felt instantly in game 1. Penix Jr. looks to be the key to this Falcons' new offense being successful and the key to further unlocking London.

London now has a quarterback who knows how to get him the ball. London got his big contract this offseason, and in this game he showed Atlanta it was money well spent. All that was needed was for the quarterback play to improve, and a healthy Penix looked to be the solution to that.

If this is just a hint of what this duo can be this season in a new offense, what was once a dead season can gain new life. We haven't even mentioned what Bijan Robinson also did on the ground against the Green Bay Packers. This Falcons offense has a chance to be special. Drake London will be a huge part of that.

Thursday night's win felt like the beginning of a new season for London and the Falcons. Drake London is now in position to have a great individual season and be a part of a team that could start winning consistently.
